subject: Post-call: capacity scan & streaming constraints for Parcelly
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Petrova <anya@parcelly.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: capacity scan & streaming constraints for Parcelly

Hi Anya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights
- Primary objective: make Parcelly's in-app summarization feature reliably low-latency for chat and streaming use-cases while keeping unit cost predictable.
- Current metrics you shared: median request ~420 tokens, median QPS during business hours ~8 QPS, recent peak window ~120 QPS (sustained ~90s), and streaming session concurrency peaks around 30–40 active sessions.
- Streaming behavior: clients stream incremental user messages and expect TTFB (time-to-first-byte) <300ms for the initial chunk, and per-token incremental latency to stay under ~50ms in production.

Open technical clarifications we need from Parcelly (please send these when you can):
1) Sample traffic (CSV): timestamps, request_id, tokens_in_request, streaming_flag, observed_client-side latency. You mentioned you can share an export — thanks in advance.
2) Payload sizes: percentiles for tokens/request (p50/p90/p99) and proportion of streaming vs batch.
3) Long-tail behavior: any abuse/spikes you’ve seen (e.g., bots, scheduled bulk jobs) and whether those should be treated as separate traffic classes.

Preliminary Redwood asks / assumptions for sizing
- Baseline SLO target (draft): 95th pct end-to-end latency <= 400ms for non-streaming; TTFB <= 300ms and incremental per-token latency <= 50ms for streaming. Confirm if this aligns with your product goals.
- For initial capacity planning we’ll map your QPS+tokens to tokens/sec and model two modes: steady-state baseline and 3x short burst headroom for 1–3 minute crest events.

Next steps (proposed)
- Anya: share sample-traffic.csv + any security docs (SOC/Security QA) by EOD Wed 10/7.
- Redwood (Karthik + Marissa): produce an initial sizing spreadsheet and cost estimate within 48 hours of receiving traffic.
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive to walk sizing assumptions and streaming kernel choices (suggest Thurs 10/8 or Fri 10/9).

Attachments: I’ll link the sizing template and HubSpot deal after this mail.

Thanks — Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine — appreciate the crisp recap. Confirming we’ll share the traffic export and a short document with percentile breakdowns. Quick clarifications from our side: 

Traffic notes (from our analytics team) — sample snapshot (local timezone):
- Typical day baseline: 6–10 QPS (median 8 QPS).
- Peak incident last week: burst up to 120 QPS for ~90s (no upstream backoff, clients kept retrying).
- Tokens/request: p50=420, p90=1,100, p99=4,200.
- Streaming usage: ~28% of requests are interactive streaming sessions; these sessions average 12s and typically push ~2–6 incremental chunks.
- Concurrency observed: sustained concurrency ~12–18, peak concurrency ~35.

We’re attaching sample-traffic.csv and the standard security-qa.pdf. Two asks for Redwood:
1) Can you show a clear mapping from tokens/sec to GPU count (rough order of magnitude) and separate streaming vs non-streaming headroom?
2) If we commit to a Dedicated pool, what would the autoscale/cooldown recommendations be to avoid oscillation during the 90s crest events?

We’ll aim to get the files to you by EOD Wed 10/7. Happy to take the deep-dive Thurs 10/8 10:00am PT.

—Anya
Product Ops | Parcelly Logistics
anya@parcelly.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Post-call recap: capacity scan & streaming constraints for Parcelly

Anya — good data, thanks. High-level preliminary sizing and operational notes (attached as redwood-sizing-estimate.xlsx):

Sizing assumptions we used (ballpark — will refine with raw CSV):
- Model family: 13B-class optimized inference (quantized) as baseline for quality/cost tradeoff.
- Per-GPU steady throughput: ~350k tokens/sec for batched non-streaming workloads (varies with sequence length); for streaming workloads where TTFB matters, effective tokens/sec drops — assume ~100k tokens/sec per GPU when honoring <300ms TTFB with small chunking.
- Mapping to your traffic: baseline steady-state tokens/sec ~= median_tokens_per_request * baseline_qps = 420 * 8 = 3360 tokens/sec. Peak crest tokens/sec ~= p90/p99 mix during your 120 QPS event — worst-case instantaneous tokens/sec estimate ~120 * 1100 = 132k tokens/sec.

Initial GPU count estimate (conservative):
- Steady baseline: 3360 tokens/sec -> negligible (<<1 GPU). We’d recommend 1x small footprint instance for warm paths to satisfy latency SLO and maintain warm KV cache.
- Peak crest (sustained 90s at ~132k tokens/sec): with streaming penalty, assume 100k tokens/sec per GPU -> ~2 GPUs to cover crest with ~20% headroom. For safety and autoscale margin, propose Dedicated pool of 3 GPUs with autoscale to 5 for extreme events.

Operational recommendations:
- Autoscale policy: target CPU/GPU utilization threshold 60–70% with a 45–60s stabilization window to avoid mid-crest oscillation. Use rapid scale-up (20–30s) and conservative cool-down (180–300s).
- Cache & batching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt fragments and set burst-aware batching that prefers small batch sizes for streaming to meet TTFB.
- Canary routing: route a small subset (5%) of production streaming traffic to the Dedicated pool initially to validate latency before increasing traffic share.

Answers to your asks:
1) tokens/sec -> GPU: see attached sheet with model-specific throughput rows (we'll refine after we get the CSV).
2) Dedicated autoscale recommendation: aggressive scale-up (start new instance when sustained >65% utilization for 15s), cool-down 3–5 minutes to avoid flip-flop during short crests.

Next steps
- We’ll finalize the sizing workbook within 24h of ingesting the CSV.
- Jasmine/Karthik: run the Thurs 10/8 10:00am PT deep-dive; Marissa will bring ops checklists and perf playbook.

Attachments: redwood-sizing-estimate.xlsx

—Karthik
